The magnitudes of the other visible integer points such as k=-5,-4,-1,1,4 are 0. In the lower phase spectrum ∠a_k, the phases of k=-3,-2,2,3 are all drawn at -π; the coefficient at k=0 lies on the real axis, with phase 0. Reasoning: Comparing positive and negative frequencies in pairs, |a_{-2}|=|a_2|=2, |a_{-3}|=|a_3|=3, and the zero coefficients are also symmetric about k=0. In terms of phase, both the positive and negative sides are -π; conjugate symmetry requires ∠a_{-k}=-∠a_k mod 2π, and -(-π)=π≡-π mod 2π, so the phase relationship satisfies conjugate symmetry. The DC term a_0=1∠0 is a real number. Therefore the Fourier series coefficients satisfy a_{-k}=a_k^*, so the periodic signal x(t) is a purely real signal.

method.method_draft: First describe the plots: identify all nonzero coefficient magnitudes and their phases. Verify that each positive-index coefficient has a matching negative-index coefficient with the same magnitude. Then check the phase relation modulo 2π: the phase -π on both sides is compatible with conjugate symmetry because -(-π)=π≡-π. Confirm the DC coefficient is real. Conclude that the coefficients are conjugate symmetric, hence the periodic signal is purely real: x(t)∈R.

method.method_draft: Convert each nonzero plotted coefficient from magnitude-phase form into a complex number. The phase -π makes the k=±2 coefficients equal to -2 and the k=±3 coefficients equal to -3, while a_0=1. Substitute only these terms into the inverse Fourier series: x(t)=1-2(e^{j2ω0t}+e^{-j2ω0t})-3(e^{j3ω0t}+e^{-j3ω0t}). Combine exponentials into cosines to get x(t)=1-4cos(2ω0t)-6cos(3ω0t), a real-valued function. Therefore x(t)∈R.
